_description: Every place this server refuses a caller because its build is older than the contract it answers. scripts/check-client-version-compatibility.mjs fails when a refusal appears that is not listed here, when an entry names a site that no longer refuses anything, or when a refusal does not name the version it needs. A forced update is a security or correctness decision taken once, not a release habit, so the list is short and every entry says what it refuses and what the caller does about it.

refusals.refuses: A caller that names an API contract version below the advertised floor. A caller that names no version at all is served, because the builds in the field predate the header.
refusals.remedy: The sentence names the contract version the caller sent and the one this deployment needs, and the advertisement carries latest, minimumSupported and unsupportedBelow so a client can decide before it is refused.

refusals.refuses: A sync push or pull whose declared protocol version is under the floor the shared contract sets, checked before the batch is parsed so the caller reads a sentence rather than a field list.
refusals.remedy: The sentence names the protocol the caller speaks and the one chat sync now needs, so the client knows which release to take rather than retrying forever.

refusals.refuses: A memory sync exchange whose declared protocol version is under the floor the shared contract sets.
refusals.remedy: The sentence names the protocol the caller speaks and the one memory sync now needs, so the client knows which release to take rather than retrying forever.

refusals.refuses: A project source upload from a client that sends no content checksum. Version 1 of that exchange authorized a storage key and nothing about its content, so honouring it would hand back an unbound upload url.
refusals.remedy: The body carries requiredUploadProtocolVersion beside the sentence, and the upgrade is one field the client already computes for registration.
